key_insight: AI decision support for nurse-led teledermoscopy was associated with substantially higher malignancy detection and more escalated management recommendations across over 1.1 million lesions.
clinical_relevance: If validated prospectively, real-time AI support could help nurse-led skin cancer screening catch more suspicious lesions while standardizing referral and follow-up decisions.
method: Real-world multi-site comparison of AI-assisted vs standard nurse-led teledermoscopy clinics in New Zealand and Australia.
Nurses captured dermoscopic images and forwarded selected lesions; teledermatologists provided the reference diagnosis.
Analysis included 1,102,382 lesions from 98,422 patients across 577 sites, adjusted for nurse experience.
evidence_signal: AI-assisted screening showed 25.5 vs 15.7 malignancies per 1,000 lesions, with adjusted odds ratio 1.73 (95% CI 1.68-1.77).
watch_item: The study was observational and non-randomized, so the benefit is associational and needs prospective outcome-based confirmation.
paper_title: AI-assisted nurse-led skin cancer screening in a teledermoscopy framework: a multi-site evaluation with one million lesions
